- Improve search relevance on product pages and support KB results with a learned reranker on top of embeddings + sparse retrieval.
- Measure gains using recall@k and NDCG; aim for >10% relative lift over current baseline.

2) Technical follow-ups (we can pair on a short tech session)

- Routing and fallbacks: recommend primary routing to the high-quality dense model with a cheaper fallback model for peak traffic.
- Outputs & tool calling: reranker responses can include structured scores and token-level snippets for explainability; we also support tool-calling-style metadata in the response.
- Embeddings + reranker stack: typical flow is candidate generation with embeddings (top 100), then rerank with Redwood ranking endpoint (top_k configurable).
- Evaluation: we'll propose an eval plan (attached) with suggested metrics (recall@k, ndcg@k, mrr, precision@k) and an A/B rollout strategy.

3) Attachment: redwood_reranker_integration_guide.pdf + initial eval plan (acme_eval_plan.xlsx) attached.

Hey Alex / team —

Thanks for the details. Quick technical notes ahead of the pairing: 

1) API behavior & top_k
- Our ranking API accepts a top_k parameter up to 200 for dense rerankers. Typical pattern: candidate generator returns N (e.g., 100) candidates, then rerank top_k (we commonly set top_k=10 for final UX).
- We support a request-level timeout and a best-effort response: if the reranker times out, Redwood can return the highest-scoring subset computed so far plus a partial flag in metadata so you can decide to fall back to baseline.

2) Latency & capacity
- With Dedicated capacity we can meet p95 < 120ms for top_k <= 20 on our recommended model family (quantized to 8-bit). For top_k > 50 expect higher CPU/KV cache pressure; we can show perf profiles in the pairing.

3) SDK & auth
- Python example (pseudo):

  from redwood import Client
  client = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
  resp = client.ranking.rerank(model="redwood-re-ranker-v1",
                              query="best running shoes for trail",
                              candidates=[{"id": "c1", "text": "..."}, ...],
                              top_k=10,
                              timeout_ms=100)
  # resp.ranked -> list of {id,score,explain} 

- SDKs handle retries, retries-on-5xx, and streaming partial results. For Private deployments we also support mTLS + customer key rotation.

4) Structured output & explainability
- The reranker can attach structured fields: score, normalized_score, token_highlights, and optional provenance pointers to the source doc id. This works well for UI-level highlights and moderation hooks.

5) Eval metrics & scripts
- Recommended metrics: recall@K (candidate generation quality), ndcg@K (final ranking quality), mrr, and precision@K. For significance testing we suggest bootstrap sampling or paired t-tests across queries.
- We'll share a small evaluation kit (python scripts + example notebooks) that compute ndcg@k given relevance judgments. See attached acme_eval_plan.xlsx with splits we recommend: 70/15/15 (train/dev/test) but if you're only doing offline eval the dev/test split of 50/50 on labeled queries is fine.

6) Next steps
- Propose a 45-min technical pairing Thu 14 Apr 10:00 PDT / 17:00 UTC.
- I'll bring a perf chart for top_k 5/10/20/50 + latency tradeoffs.

Happy to answer any deeper infra questions in advance.
